samples.text:
The two maps illustrates the centre of Brenton town in 2000 and today. In general, there are a lot of changes, especially the High Street became for pedestrians.

In 2000, the High Street was a road from west to east. On the north side there was shops and a town hall, and there was a park in the north-west. On the south side there were some shops, a cinema, an open-air market and a big car park in the south-east. Mill Road went from the High Street to the south.

Today, the High Street is a pedestrian zone The cinema and the market was replaced by a large shopping centre, and Mill Road has been removed. In the south-east, a bus station has been built instead of the car park. Then, a new road was built in the north. Also, a multi-storey car park is now in the north-east. The park became smaller and a play area was built next to it, and the market has moved to north of the town hall. The shops and town hall are same as before.
samples.why: Overview present but generalised · most changes reported though listed mechanically · basic linking (Then, Also) · adequate vocabulary · frequent agreement and article errors which do not impede meaning.

samples.text:
The maps compare the layout of Brenton town centre in 2000 with its present-day appearance. Overall, the town centre has been redesigned to favour pedestrians and public transport, with traffic being moved away from the High Street to a new road in the north.

The most significant change is that the High Street, a road running from west to east in 2000, has since been pedestrianised. At the same time, a new road, New Road, has been built across the north of the town. The shops on both sides of the street, as well as the town hall, have been kept.

South of the High Street, the cinema and the open-air market have been demolished to make room for a large shopping centre, and Mill Road, which used to lead south from the High Street, no longer exist. The car park in the south-east has been replaced by a bus station, accessed by a short road from the east.

In the north-west, the park has been reduced in size, with a play area built alongside it. The market has relocated to a site north of the town hall, while a multi-storey car park has appeared in the north-east.
samples.why: Clear overview · changes well organised by area with logical progression · varied cohesive devices · good vocabulary (pedestrianised, relocated) · largely accurate with one or two minor slips.

samples.text:
The maps illustrate how the centre of Brenton was reorganised between 2000 and the present day. The overriding change is that the central High Street has been closed to traffic, with a new road built in the north, while several facilities have been replaced or relocated.

Several features remain as they were: the town hall on the northern side of the High Street, the two rows of shops flanking it and the block of shops in the south-west. The High Street, however, has been converted into a pedestrian zone, and New Road now crosses the northern part of the town from west to east. Meanwhile, the park in the north-west has shrunk, and part of its former area has become a children's play area.

To the south, the cinema and the open-air market have been swept away to accommodate a sizeable shopping centre, and Mill Road, which formerly ran south from the High Street, has disappeared. The large car park in the south-east has made way for a bus station reached by a short road from the east. Parking is now provided in a multi-storey car park in the north-east, and the market occupies a smaller site immediately behind the town hall.
samples.why: Clear, well-placed overview · changes skilfully grouped into retained, northern and southern features · cohesion handled naturally · precise vocabulary (flanking, swept away, accommodate) · wide range of structures, essentially error-free.
